chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
Regarding a woman who gives a man wealth to marry her, and he marries her, he said: 'The wealth is a gift, and the private part (intimacy) is permissible.'

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private part (referring to sexual intimacy)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a woman pays a man to marry her in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that when a woman pays a man to marry her, the payment is legally classified as a gift (hibah) rather than a mandatory dowry (mahr), ensuring the marriage contract remains valid. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial arrangements in marriage, affirming that the marital bond itself renders intimacy permissible without requiring a distinct dowry transaction. The hadith highlights the distinction between contractual obligations and voluntary gifts in establishing lawful conjugal relations.
